objective_pt: Recognise and use understatement, sarcasm and self-deprecating humour ("Well, that went well", "It's not the end of the world"), and react naturally when someone is joking.

teacher.goal_pt: Compare Brazilian and English-speaking humour, especially British understatement.
prompts: Is Brazilian humour more direct or more ironic?
Has anyone ever misunderstood one of your jokes in English?
watchFor: "Joke" vs "kid": "Are you kidding?" is the natural form, not "Are you joking with me?".

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat with an ironic, flat tone, as if something has just gone wrong.
accepted: Well, that went well

exercises.instruction_pt: It's pouring with rain and your friend says "Lovely weather for a picnic." What does she mean?
options: She wants to have a picnic.
She's being sarcastic: the weather is terrible.
She thinks the rain is lovely.
exercises.explanation_pt: Sarcasm says the opposite of what is meant, often with a flat or exaggerated tone.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Você está brincando!"
accepted: You're kidding!
You're joking!
Are you kidding?
Are you kidding me?
Are you joking?
You must be joking!
You've got to be kidding!
No way!
Seriously?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Brincar" in the sense of joking is "kid" or "joke". "You're playing" means you're playing a game.
commonErrors.correction_en: You're kidding!

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Brincando comigo" is "kidding me" / "pulling my leg", not "joking with me".
commonErrors.correction_en: Are you kidding me?

teacher.goal_pt: Humour vocabulary: tongue-in-cheek, deadpan, understatement, to pull someone's leg, self-deprecating.
prompts: Do you know anyone with a deadpan sense of humour?
When did someone last pull your leg?
watchFor: "Humor" stressed as in Portuguese (hu-MOR) instead of HU-mour.
"Funny" vs "fun": a funny person makes you laugh; a fun person is enjoyable to be with.

exercises.meaning_pt: zoar alguém, fazer alguém de bobo (de brincadeira)
exercises.example_en: Relax, I'm just pulling your leg.

exercises.meaning_pt: sem expressão, com cara séria (ao fazer piada)
exercises.example_en: She has a brilliant deadpan delivery.

exercises.instruction_pt: Match each word with its meaning.

pairs.pt: eufemismo, dizer menos do que é

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Relaxa, eu só estou te zoando."
accepted: Relax, I'm just pulling your leg
Relax, I'm just kidding
Relax, I'm only joking
Relax, I'm just joking
Relax, I'm just messing with you
Chill, I'm just kidding
Don't worry, I'm just pulling your leg
Relax, I'm only kidding
Relax, I'm just teasing you

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Zoar" is "kid", "tease" or "pull someone's leg". "Play with you" sounds childish or odd.
commonErrors.correction_en: Relax, I'm just pulling your leg.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The idiom is "pull someone's leg", with "leg", not "foot".
commonErrors.correction_en: Relax, I'm just pulling your leg.

teacher.goal_pt: Intonation of sarcasm: flat or exaggerated pitch, lengthened vowels.
prompts: Say "Oh, brilliant" as if your train was just cancelled.
watchFor: Same tone for sincere and sarcastic versions, so the irony is lost.
Overacting so much that it sounds aggressive.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat sarcastically: stretch "brilliant" and keep the pitch low and flat.
exercises.prompt: Oh, brilliant. Just what I needed.
accepted: Oh, brilliant. Just what I needed

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat this understatement in a calm, dry voice.
exercises.prompt: It's not exactly the best idea I've ever heard.
accepted: It's not exactly the best idea I've ever heard
It is not exactly the best idea I have ever heard

exercises.explanation_pt: In English the stress is on the first syllable: HU-mour (/ˈhjuː.mər/), unlike "humor" in Portuguese.

teacher.goal_pt: Detect irony from context and tone, and play along.
prompts: How could you reply with a joke?
watchFor: Literal answers to jokes ("No, the weather is bad").
Missing understatement ("a bit of a problem" = a big problem).

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. How bad is the situation really?
exercises.listen: The car broke down, it started snowing and we missed the wedding. So, yeah, it was a bit of a disappointing day.
options: Actually very bad. The speaker is using understatement.
exercises.explanation_pt: "A bit of a disappointing day" after a list of disasters is classic understatement.

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen. Your friend is joking about herself. Reply light-heartedly.
exercises.listen: I tried to bake a cake yesterday and I set off the fire alarm. Twice.
accepted: Well, at least you tried!
At least the alarm works!
Well, at least you know the alarm works!
Sounds like a great success!
Master chef in the making!
Remind me never to eat your cake!
Practice makes perfect!
So it went well, then!
That sounds like my kind of cooking!
Twice? Impressive!

commonErrors.explanation_pt: She's joking about herself, so a serious apology misses the tone. Play along: "At least the alarm works!"
commonErrors.correction_en: Well, at least you know the alarm works!

exercises.instruction_pt: Listen and reply with an understatement about the weather.
exercises.listen: Have you seen it outside? It's like a hurricane out there.
accepted: It's a bit windy, isn't it?
Yeah, it's a little breezy
Just a bit breezy, then
Bit windy, isn't it?
Not exactly beach weather, is it?
It's not ideal, is it?
A little blustery, yes
Yeah, slightly windy
Yes, it's a bit wild out there

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The Portuguese "né?" becomes a question tag in English: "It's a bit windy, isn't it?", not "windy, no?".
commonErrors.correction_en: It's a bit windy, isn't it?

commonErrors.explanation_pt: That's accurate, but the task asks for understatement: say less than it is ("a bit windy").
commonErrors.correction_en: It's a bit windy, isn't it?

teacher.goal_pt: Tell a funny story using self-deprecation and understatement; react to the teacher's irony.
prompts: Tell me about your worst cooking (or DIY) disaster.
(Teacher uses sarcasm.) Did you get it?
What kind of jokes don't translate well from Portuguese?

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Não sou exatamente o melhor motorista do mundo."
accepted: I'm not exactly the best driver in the world
I'm not exactly the world's best driver
I'm not exactly a great driver
I'm not the best driver in the world, to be honest
Let's just say I'm not the best driver in the world
I'm not exactly the best driver ever

commonErrors.explanation_pt: With superlatives and places, English uses "in": "the best driver in the world".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm not exactly the best driver in the world.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Motorist" exists but is formal (news reports). In conversation, "motorista" is "driver".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm not exactly the best driver in the world.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Não é o fim do mundo."
accepted: It's not the end of the world
It isn't the end of the world
That's not the end of the world
It's hardly the end of the world
Well, it's not the end of the world

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Keep both articles: "the end of the world".
commonErrors.correction_en: It's not the end of the world.

exercises.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to make a self-deprecating joke.
accepted: Let's just say cooking isn't my strong point

exercises.instruction_pt: Tell a short funny story about yourself in about a minute, using understatement or self-deprecation.
exercises.prompt_en: Tell me about a time when something went hilariously wrong for you. Don't be afraid to laugh at yourself.
guidelines_pt: Use self-deprecation: "Let's just say I'm not the most...".
Use understatement for the worst moment: "It was a bit of a disaster."
End with a punchline or "Well, at least...".

teacher.goal_pt: Recycle humour vocabulary and check the learner can switch between literal and ironic readings.
prompts: Say something sarcastic about Monday mornings.
watchFor: Flat intonation that hides the irony.

exercises.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Ele tem um senso de humor muito seco."
accepted: He has a very dry sense of humour
He has a very dry sense of humor
He's got a very dry sense of humour
He's got a really dry sense of humor
He has a really dry sense of humour
His sense of humour is very dry

commonErrors.explanation_pt: No article: "a sense of humour".
commonErrors.correction_en: He has a very dry sense of humour.

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Adjectives go before the noun: "a very dry sense of humour".
commonErrors.correction_en: He has a very dry sense of humour.

exercises.sentence: Don't take it seriously, I'm only pulling your ___.
accepted: leg

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The idiom is "pull someone's leg".
commonErrors.correction_en: Don't take it seriously, I'm only pulling your leg.

options: This is the worst day of my entire life!
Losing my wallet was slightly inconvenient.
I'm so happy I could fly!
exercises.explanation_pt: Understatement makes something sound less serious than it is: "slightly inconvenient" for a lost wallet.

exercises.instruction_pt: Repeat with a smile in your voice.
exercises.prompt: Well, it could have been worse.
accepted: Well, it could have been worse
It could have been worse
Well, it could've been worse

practice.example_en: Don't listen to him. He's just taking the mickey.
She gave a wry smile when the printer jammed again.
His impression of the boss had us all in stitches.

practice.meaning_pt: não ter graça, não funcionar (piada, ideia)
practice.example_en: My joke about tax returns fell flat.

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with a flat, sarcastic tone.
practice.prompt: Great, another Monday. Just what I was hoping for.
accepted: Great, another Monday. Just what I was hoping for

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with a self-deprecating smile in your voice.
practice.prompt: I'm not the most organised person in the world.
accepted: I'm not the most organised person in the world
I'm not the most organized person in the world
I am not the most organised person in the world

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
accepted: The joke fell completely flat
The joke completely fell flat

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat with natural rhythm and stress.
practice.prompt: We were in stitches the whole evening.
accepted: We were in stitches the whole evening
We were in stitches all evening

practice.instruction_pt: Repeat sarcastically, as if it's pouring with rain.
accepted: Lovely weather we're having
Lovely weather we are having

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Tô brincando, relaxa!"
accepted: I'm kidding, relax
I'm only kidding, relax
I'm just kidding, relax
Just kidding, relax
I'm joking, relax
I'm only joking, chill
Relax, I'm just kidding
Relax, I'm only joking
Chill, I'm just kidding
I'm just joking, relax

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Brincar" in this sense is "kid" or "joke", not "play".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'm only kidding, relax!

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Ele não é exatamente um gênio."
accepted: He's not exactly a genius
He isn't exactly a genius
He's not exactly the sharpest tool in the box
He is not exactly a genius
He's hardly a genius
He's no genius
He's not what you'd call a genius

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The ironic phrase is "not exactly": "He's not exactly a genius".
commonErrors.correction_en: He's not exactly a genius.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this ironically in natural English: "Que maravilha, perdi o ônibus de novo."
accepted: Brilliant, I missed the bus again
Great, I missed the bus again
Fantastic, I've missed the bus again
Brilliant, I've missed the bus again
Wonderful, I missed the bus again
Great, missed the bus again
Perfect, I missed the bus again
Just great, I missed the bus again
Lovely, I've missed the bus again

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Perder" a bus or a flight is "miss", not "lose".
commonErrors.correction_en: Brilliant, I missed the bus again.

practice.instruction_pt: Say this in natural English: "Você tá me zoando?"
accepted: Are you pulling my leg
Are you having me on
Are you kidding me
Are you joking
You're pulling my leg, aren't you
Are you messing with me
Are you taking the mickey
Are you winding me up

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Zoar alguém" can be "make fun of someone", not "make fun with".
commonErrors.correction_en: Are you making fun of me?

practice.instruction_pt: Say this with dry humour in natural English: "Pelo menos não choveu... muito."
accepted: At least it didn't rain much
Well, at least it didn't rain much
At least it didn't rain too much
At least it didn't pour
At least it didn't rain that much
Look on the bright side, it didn't rain much

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Past negative uses "didn't" + base verb: "it didn't rain".
commonErrors.correction_en: At least it didn't rain much.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and answer with ironic understatement: it went badly.
practice.listen: So, how was the job interview?
accepted: Well, it could have gone better
It could have gone better
Let's just say it wasn't my finest hour
Not my finest moment
It wasn't exactly a triumph
Let's just say I won't be holding my breath
It didn't go brilliantly
I wouldn't call it a success
Put it this way, I won't be getting a call back
It wasn't my best performance

commonErrors.explanation_pt: For a past event use "could have gone better".
commonErrors.correction_en: Well, it could have gone better.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and respond with self-deprecating humour.
practice.listen: I heard you locked yourself out again!
accepted: Yes, I'm a genius, aren't I
Guilty as charged
What can I say, it's a talent
Yep, my memory is legendary
I know. I should get a medal
Don't remind me
It's a gift, really
Yes, I'm clearly not the brightest
Yeah, I'm hopeless
What can I say? I'm a professional
Yes, I locked myself out again. Classic me

commonErrors.explanation_pt: When subject and object are the same person, use "myself": "I locked myself out".
commonErrors.correction_en: I locked myself out again.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen and answer sarcastically.
practice.listen: Did you enjoy the three-hour meeting?
accepted: Oh, I loved every minute of it
Absolutely, best three hours of my life
Oh yes, it was thrilling
It was the highlight of my week
I couldn't get enough of it
Oh, it was riveting
What's not to love
Oh, I was on the edge of my seat
Loved it. Can't wait for the next one

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The fixed phrase is "every minute of it".
commonErrors.correction_en: Oh, I loved every minute of it.

practice.instruction_pt: Tell a short, funny story about yourself in about a minute.
practice.prompt_en: Tell me about a time something embarrassing happened to you.
guidelines_pt: Use self-deprecating humour: "I'm not exactly the most...".
Add an ironic comment: "Well, that went well."
Use understatement for the worst moment: "It was a bit awkward."
End lightly: "Looking back, it's quite funny."

practice.instruction_pt: Role-play: banter with a colleague, using irony and understatement.
practice.scene_pt: It's Monday morning at the office. You slept badly and a colleague notices.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Answer ironically that you've had a whole four hours of sleep.
accepted: Yeah, a whole four hours of sleep
I know, I had a whole four hours of sleep
Well, I got a whole four hours of sleep
I've had a whole four hours of sleep, so I'm fresh as a daisy
Thanks, I had a whole four hours of sleep
Yep, a whole four hours of sleep. I'm a new person

commonErrors.explanation_pt: Use the noun: "four hours of sleep".
commonErrors.correction_en: A whole four hours of sleep.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say not exactly. Your neighbour's dog decided to sing all night.
accepted: Not exactly. My neighbour's dog decided to sing all night
Not exactly. My neighbor's dog decided to sing all night
Not exactly. The neighbour's dog decided to sing all night
Not exactly. My neighbour's dog decided to sing all night long
Not quite. My neighbour's dog decided to sing all night
Not really. My neighbour's dog decided to sing all night

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "A noite toda" is "all night", without "the".
commonErrors.correction_en: My neighbour's dog sang all night.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Oh no. Well, at least you've got the presentation this afternoon to look forward to.

turns.speaker: you
turns.cue_pt: Say sarcastically: oh yes, you can hardly contain your excitement.
accepted: Oh yes, I can hardly contain my excitement
Oh yes, I can barely contain my excitement
Oh, I can hardly contain my excitement
Yes, I can hardly contain my excitement
Oh yes, I can't contain my excitement
Oh yes, I can hardly wait

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Excitação" (empolgação) is "excitement".
commonErrors.correction_en: I can hardly contain my excitement.

turns.speaker: partner
turns.text: Don't worry, I'll bring you a coffee. A large one.

turns.speaker: you
accepted: I'd be eternally grateful
I would be eternally grateful
You're a lifesaver. I'd be eternally grateful
I'd be forever grateful
You're a star. I'd be eternally grateful
Thanks, I'd be eternally grateful

commonErrors.explanation_pt: "Agradecido" is "grateful".
commonErrors.correction_en: I'd be eternally grateful.

practice.instruction_pt: After a disaster, someone says "Well, that was a total success." What are they being?
practice.explanation_pt: Saying the opposite of what is obviously true, with a flat tone, is sarcasm.

practice.instruction_pt: Which is an example of understatement?
options: Calling a hurricane "the worst storm in history"
practice.explanation_pt: Understatement makes something sound much smaller than it is, usually for humour.

practice.instruction_pt: Listen. What kind of humour is this?
practice.listen: Oh, I'm hopeless at cooking. I once managed to burn a pot of water.
practice.explanation_pt: The speaker jokes about her own lack of skill, which is self-deprecating humour.

practice.instruction_pt: Complete with one word.
practice.sentence: Don't take it seriously. He's only pulling your ___.
accepted: leg

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The idiom is "pull someone's leg".
commonErrors.correction_en: He's only pulling your leg.

practice.instruction_pt: Complete with one word.
practice.sentence: His impression of the teacher was so funny that we were all in ___.
accepted: stitches

commonErrors.explanation_pt: The idiom is "in stitches".
commonErrors.correction_en: We were all in stitches.

practice.instruction_pt: Put the words in order to make an ironic understatement.
accepted: It wasn't exactly the best day of my life
